bundles.evidenceText: this cause must be an uncaused change less time less and immaterial being which created the universe
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the universe began, requires a transcendent cause, and that this cause is uncaused, timeless, spaceless, and immaterial. This supports the exact pro subsidiary bridge that the universe’s finite beginning and causal need imply such a transcendent cause; if the proposition is true, that bridge becomes more credible. The narrower subsidiary bridge is selected rather than the pro central bridge because the move does not assert cumulative convergence across all five evidential lines.

bundles.evidenceText: scientific beliefs do not depend on cultural indoctrination for their acceptance and transmission
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that scientific progress rests on observation and critical scrutiny whereas religious beliefs are culturally transmitted and geographically variable. That proposition can remain true without changing the credibility of any stated bridge concerning Kalam causation, fine-tuning, resurrection, evil, or the cumulative five-line inference, so there is no exact route contact. The nearest competitor is support for the con central bridge, but criticism of religious belief formation does not itself establish that the five specified evidential inferences are underdetermined or face contrary empirical evidence.

bundles.evidenceText: the world we see just doesn't match up to what you'd expect from a perfect God
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the observed world, including evil and morally objectionable divine conduct, is contrary to what a perfect God would lead us to expect. This supports the con subsidiary bridge that the world’s evil and opaque divine presence are empirically less expected under a morally perfect Christian God than under skeptical atheism; its truth directly increases that bridge’s credibility. The con motion bridge is excluded because the expressed reason is specifically the evidential problem of evil, not a complete assessment of all cited evidence.

bundles.evidenceText: it may well be that only in a world suffused with natural evil as well as moral evil then the maximum number of people would freely come God
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that God may permit natural and moral evil because such a world could maximize the number of people freely entering relationship with God. This attacks the con subsidiary bridge that evil is empirically less expected from a morally perfect Christian God, because the proposed divine purpose limits the inference from evil to divine improbability; if true, that bridge becomes less credible. No-contact is the nearest excluded candidate, but the move directly answers the bridge’s necessary expectancy inference rather than merely discussing conduct associated with Christianity.
